speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA) variant or Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) with behavioral variant features, given the prominent personality changes, executive dysfunction, and gait instability in a 44-year-old. However, the acute onset of leg weakness and falls raises concern for a structural lesion (e.g., paraneoplastic syndrome, autoimmune encephalitis, or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome - PRES). I will request MRI of the brain with and without contrast to evaluate for structural abnormalities, white matter changes, or mass lesions. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_WithAndWithoutContrast
